newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - April 2.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Industrial sales recorded real decline in February compared with the same period in 1996. According to the Czech Statistical Bureau sales also declined 3.6 percent month-on-month.
- SPT Telecom recorded operational profits of 32 billion crowns, a growth of 26 percent.
- The finance ministry announced that the state budget is in deficit by 8.5 billion crowns. For January-February the deficit reached 6.7 billion crowns.
- Ironworks Trinecke Zelezarny is negotiating with ProWin, the majority owner of Poldi Ocel for a contract that would renew production at the Poldi steelworks.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The government plans to announce unpopular economic reform measures by the middle of April. Measures being considered include a freeze on wages and possible import tariffs on consumer and luxury items.
- Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy has yet to submit a plan to the finance ministry on how to privatise the country's coal and petrochemical industries.
- The ruling Civic Democratic Party (ODS) has admitted that it has received donations from Iceberg, the controversial brokerage firm.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Assets of CS fond are not definitely lost according to its legal representatives. The law firm Vana, Pergl and Parners claims that there is still a good chance that the 1.3 billion crowns which disappeared from the fond in March may be recovered.

PRAVO - The Association of Pharmaceutical Distributors has decided to stop supplying four hospitals with non-essential drugs. The reason for the stoppage was that the hospitals were not paying their bills.
